answer: 5.1.2 [Q#9: "the embeddings device" — there is no such device today; embeddings go through the inference proxy's embed verb. A device of its own to come?] --- wow. ok, this is the first device after you and cairn. why? let me give you the 100ft on the memory again: one long tree of nodes id=row. individual tables for each tree. weights are in the leaves. links are bidirectional. trees are calved at dominant attractors when > 5K leaves. it's a deterministic code shear. different trees can index the same data in different ways. each tree asks a question. for a given question, any string can be sent to the embeddings generator. string + question. that word graph returns a histogram that is the embedding, the weighted path followed by the tree. this embedding can be searched with LIKE. a memory node can carry any number of embeddings, however we don't routinely generate every possible embedding it would become a sea of useless data. instead my mind runs science fiction past questions like 'how might that work' looking for things i could use later from other domains. that's how our memory's INTENTIONS work. so the embeddings generator comes even before the librarian. because the librarian will be it's biggest user
